content:
(PRATIṢṬHĀ-MUHŪRTA-VICĀRA)

मासेषु फाल्गुने चैत्रे ज्येष्ठे वैशाखतिष्ययोः ।
उत्तमं श्रावणे मध्यं कार्तिकाश्वयुजोरपि ।।
अधमं भाद्रपादेपि तथाषाढे च मासि वै ।
मार्गशीर्षञ्च माघञ्च वर्जयित्वा विचक्षणः ॥
शेषेष्वपि च कर्तव्यं त्वरितेनेति मे मतिः ।
शुक्लपक्षे तथा कृष्णे विभागे त्रयंशकं विना।
रेवतीरोहिणीतिष्यस्वाती श्रवणवासवाः।
चित्राश्विनीशतभिषक्पुनर्वस्वैन्दवाश्शुभाः।।
कृत्तिका नवमी शस्ता दुर्गायाः कार्तिकेपि च।
प्रतिष्ठा भास्वतश्श्स्ता रवौ सिंहगते तथा ।
फाल्गुनोत्तरफल्गुन्योः श्रीप्रतिष्ठा प्रशस्यते ।
रौद्रं रुद्रप्रतिष्ठायां माघमासं च कथ्यते ।।
श्रवणं चाश्चयुङ्‌मासे मत्स्यादिस्थापनाविधौ ।
अनन्धकाणनक्षत्रे करणे च शुभोदये ॥
त्रिजन्मसु प्रतिष्ठा स्याद्यजमानस्य भूपतेः ।
काव्यजीवज्ञवारांशहोराद्रेकाणकांस्तथा ।।

बधुवारांशकादींस्तु प्रशंसन्ति मनीषिणः ।
षष्ट्यष्टमीपर्वरिक्तानन्दादिषु तिथिष्वपि ॥
चरेषु करणेष्वेव शुभयोगेष्वविष्टिषु।
तिथिवारर्क्षयोगादिदोषैरपि विवर्जिते ॥
रव्यादिषु शुभस्थेषु तथा रिक्तेष्टमे ग्रहैः ।
त्रिषडायगतैः पापै शुभैः केन्द्रत्रिकोणगैः ॥
शुभैर्युक्तैतथवा दृष्टे कामशुक्रविवर्जिते ।
प्रतिष्ठां देवदेवस्य कुर्यात्पूर्वाङ्ग एव वै ॥
summary: This appendix, titled "Excerpts from Kriyādhikāra," presents a detailed treatise on the selection of auspicious timings (Muhūrta) for the consecration of deities (Pratiṣṭhā). It provides a comprehensive set of astrological rules, outlining favorable and unfavorable lunar months, lunar days (tithis), lunar mansions (nakṣatras), and planetary configurations. The text categorizes months as best, medium, and avoidable, lists generally auspicious nakṣatras, and provides specific recommendations for the installation of certain deities like Durgā, Sūrya (Bhāsvat), Śrī, and Rudra. It also details the required placement of benefic and malefic planets in the astrological chart for the ceremony, the conditions of the ascendant, and other criteria to ensure a successful and meritorious consecration.
purpose: The purpose of this text is to serve as a guide for determining the most astrologically suitable time (muhūrta) for the 'pratiṣṭhā' or consecration ceremony of a deity's idol. It provides the necessary astrological parameters to be considered by priests and patrons (yajamāna) to maximize the sanctity, power, and auspiciousness of the installed deity.
key_information: Classification of Months: Months are categorized into Uttama (best: Phālguna, Caitra, Jyeṣṭha, Vaiśākha, Pauṣa), Madhya (medium: Śrāvaṇa, Kārtika, Āśvina), and Adhama/Varjya (to be avoided: Bhādrapāda, Āṣāḍha, Mārgaśīrṣa, Māgha).

Auspicious Nakṣatras: A list of generally auspicious nakṣatras is provided, including Revatī, Rohiṇī, Puṣya (Tiṣya), Svātī, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā (Vāsava), Citrā, Aśvinī, Śatabhiṣak, Punarvasu, and Mṛgaśīrṣa (Aindava).

Deity-Specific Timings: Specific timings are recommended for certain deities. For example, Kṛttikā nakṣatra for Durgā, Sun in Leo for Sūrya, Phālguna month and Uttara Phālgunī nakṣatra for Śrī, and Māgha month for Rudra.

General Astrological Rules: The text advises using the Śuklapakṣa (bright fortnight), avoiding certain tithis (6th, 8th, Riktā, etc.), choosing auspicious yogas and karaṇas, and ensuring the muhūrta is free from various astrological defects.

Planetary Positions (Horoscopy): It specifies ideal planetary placements for the ceremony: benefic planets in Kendra (1,4,7,10) or Trikona (1,5,9) houses; malefic planets in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses; and the 8th house being vacant. It also advises against having Venus in the 7th house.
Considerations for the Patron (Yajamāna): The consecration should consider the 'trijanma' nakṣatras (birth star and related ones) of the patron.

tables_and_data.description: Classification of Lunar Months for Pratiṣṭhā
tables_and_data.data_summary:
The text classifies the twelve lunar months based on their suitability for consecration ceremonies. 
- Uttama (Best): Phālguna, Caitra, Jyeṣṭha, Vaiśākha, Pauṣa (Tiṣya).
- Madhya (Medium): Śrāvaṇa, Kārtika, Āśvina (Āśvayuja).
- Adhama/Varjya (Inferior/To be Avoided): Bhādrapāda, Āṣāḍha, Mārgaśīrṣa, Māgha (with an exception noted for Rudra's consecration in Māgha).

A list of generally favorable nakṣatras for consecration is provided: Revatī, Rohiṇī, Puṣya, Svātī, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Citrā, Aśvinī, Śatabhiṣak, Punarvasu, and Mṛgaśīrṣa. Kṛttikā is specifically mentioned as auspicious for the consecration of Goddess Durgā.
